question: Let $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be defined by $f(x)=x^2+1$. Examine whether $f$ is one-one. Justify your answer.
explanation:
Selection of distinct elements
Consider $1,-1\in\mathbb{Z}$, where
$$1\ne-1.$$

Comparison of images
We have
$$f(1)=1^2+1=2$$
and
$$f(-1)=(-1)^2+1=2.$$
Thus, $f(1)=f(-1)$ although $1\ne-1$.

Conclusion
Two distinct elements of the domain have the same image. Hence, $f$ is not one-one.

options.B: $f$ is one-one because every integer has exactly one square
options.C: $f$ is one-one because $x^2+1$ is always positive
